cards.front: Recall a key point about Dance Structure & Form
cards.back: Dance structure is how a piece is organised — the overall shape and order of sections

cards.front: Recall a key point about Dance Structure & Form
cards.back: Binary form has two contrasting sections: A then B (e.g. fast then slow)

cards.front: Recall a key point about Dance Structure & Form
cards.back: Ternary form has three sections: ABA — the opening section returns after a contrast

cards.front: Recall a key point about Dance Structure & Form
cards.back: Rondo form alternates a main theme with different episodes: ABACADA

cards.front: Recall a key point about Dance Structure & Form
cards.back: Narrative structure tells a story with a beginning, middle and end in chronological order

cards.front: Recall a key point about Dance Structure & Form
cards.back: Abstract structure is organised around movement ideas without a storyline

cards.front: Recall a key point about Dance Structure & Form
cards.back: Thematic structure develops and varies one or more movement themes throughout

cards.front: Recall a key point about Dance Structure & Form
cards.back: The choice of structure affects how the audience experiences and understands the dance

cards.front: Recall a key point about Dance Structure & Form
cards.back: Choreographers choose a structure that best supports their intention

cards.front: Recall a key point about Dance Structure & Form
cards.back: Some professional works combine more than one structural form

cards.front: Recall a key point about Dance Structure & Form
cards.back: In AQA 8236 NEA, you must identify and justify your chosen structure

cards.front: Recall a key point about Dance Structure & Form
cards.back: Structure is often compared to musical form — many dance structures borrow from music
